content: Apple mint, also known as woolly mint, is scientifically classified as Mentha suaveolens (with synonyms including Mentha rotundifolia and Mentha insularis Req.). This plant belongs to the mint genus Mentha and is native to regions of southern and western Europe as well as the western Mediterranean. It is a herbaceous, upright perennial plant that is commonly cultivated either as a culinary herb or as ground cover. Apple mint typically grows to a height of 40 to 100 cm and spreads through rhizomes, forming clonal colonies. Its foliage is light green, with opposite, sessile leaves that are oblong to nearly ovate in shape, measuring 3 to 5 cm in length and 2 to 4 cm in width. The leaves are somewhat hairy on their upper surface and downy underneath, with serrated edges. During mid to late summer, apple mint produces flowers that are light purple-pink in color. Cultivation and Uses Apple mint is an aesthetically pleasing herb that is often used as an ornamental plant. It is hardy and easy to grow, thriving in conditions ranging from full sun to light shade. The leaves of apple mint can be utilized in various culinary applications, such as making apple mint jelly or as a flavoring in dishes like apple mint couscous. Additionally, it is frequently used to prepare mint tea, as a garnish, or as an ingredient in salads. A notable cultivar of apple mint is pineapple mint (Mentha suaveolens 'Variegata'), which is distinguished by its leaves that are banded with white. Another hybrid derived from apple mint is grapefruit mint (Mentha suaveolens x piperata).
